title: CONTROL Resonant Release Date, Early Access, and Platforms
excerpt: The verified digital and physical release schedule, platform list, early access timing, and cloud and Mac availability.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant launches first as a digital release, with physical console editions and the Mac version following on separate schedules. This guide separates the dates and storefront details that are easy to confuse.
quickAnswer: CONTROL Resonant launches digitally on September 24, 2026 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Steam, and Epic Games Store. PlayStation Digital Deluxe buyers receive 48-hour early access from September 22. Physical console editions are dated October 15, while the Mac version is planned for later in 2026.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden overlooking a paranaturally transformed Manhattan in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: When does CONTROL Resonant release?
paragraphs: The September 24 date is the worldwide digital launch date announced by Remedy. Storefront unlock times can differ by region, and the New Zealand PlayStation Store displays September 25 because of its local time zone.

rows: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Steam, Epic
Physical PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
Mac via Steam and Mac App Store
table.caption: Complete release schedule

sections.title: Confirmed platforms and services
paragraphs: The launch console versions are exclusive to the current generation: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. PC players can buy the game through Steam or the Epic Games Store. Remedy also lists GeForce NOW for launch-day cloud play.

The Xbox version supports Xbox Play Anywhere, so one digital purchase can be used across Xbox Series X|S and Xbox on PC with compatible saves and achievements. Xbox Play Anywhere is a purchase entitlement, not a Game Pass announcement.
bullets: PlayStation 5, with PS5 Pro enhancement listed on PlayStation Store
Xbox Series X|S and Xbox on PC through Xbox Play Anywhere
Windows PC through Steam and Epic Games Store
GeForce NOW cloud streaming at digital launch
Mac through Steam and the Mac App Store later in 2026

image.alt: An overhead view of a distorted Manhattan zone in CONTROL Resonant
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot. The sequel moves beyond the Oldest House into expansive Manhattan zones.

sections.title: How the 48-hour early access works
paragraphs: The PlayStation Store lists September 22 at 14:00 UTC for the Digital Deluxe Edition, which is 48 hours before the worldwide digital release. Remedy describes early access as a PlayStation Digital Deluxe benefit; it is not listed for the Steam Digital Deluxe package.
Regional store pages may convert that UTC time or show the following calendar day. Use the countdown shown by the store connected to the purchasing account as the final local unlock time.

sections.title: Platforms that are not announced
paragraphs: No PS4, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch, or Nintendo Switch 2 version has been announced. A platform omission is not proof that a port can never happen, but there is no verified release to list for those systems as of this page's update date.

sections.title: What to check before buying
bullets: Choose Digital Deluxe only if its artbook, soundtrack, artifact, resources, outfit, or PlayStation early access matter to you.
PC requires 120 GB of SSD storage across every official specification tier.
The Steam version is listed as Steam Deck compatible at launch in Remedy's developer FAQ, but a final Valve verification badge is a separate status.
A Mac release is confirmed for later in 2026, not for September 24.

title: CONTROL Resonant Gameplay Explained
excerpt: How exploration, World Quests, melee combat, Combat Abilities, executions, Resonants, and The Gap connect.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant is a third-person action RPG built around open-ended Manhattan zones and a melee-first combat loop. Remedy's official deep dives now provide enough detail to explain its major systems without inventing a launch walkthrough.
quickAnswer: Gameplay alternates between exploring handcrafted Manhattan zones, following Dylan's Journey and optional World Quests, fighting with the shape-changing Aberrant, and building a loadout from Weapon Forms, Combat Abilities, Talents, and Artifacts. Major Resonant bosses unlock new ability choices.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden fighting hostile entities on a red-lit Manhattan street

sections.title: The gameplay structure
paragraphs: Remedy describes the game as open-ended rather than as one uninterrupted open world. Manhattan is divided into large, distinct zones with their own atmosphere, encounters, lore, side activities, and secrets.

sections.title: Exploring warped Manhattan
paragraphs: The paranatural crisis has spread outside the Oldest House. Players can leave the critical path to investigate optional spaces, hidden encounters, environmental puzzles, collectibles, and narrative World Quests.

Gravity Anomalies can rotate or reorient entire spaces. They are not only visual effects: official gameplay shows Dylan navigating surfaces and perspectives that no longer obey ordinary Manhattan geometry.

image.alt: Dylan navigating a flooded space distorted by a Gravity Anomaly
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot showing traversal inside a gravity-distorted environment.

sections.title: Dylan's Journey and World Quests
paragraphs: Dylan's Journey is Remedy's name for the main campaign. World Quests are substantial optional stories found in Manhattan's zones rather than simple checklist errands.

Zoe De Vera, an FBC field agent assigned as Dylan's handler, speaks with him during exploration. Remedy says the dialogue runs seamlessly, so story context can arrive without repeatedly cutting away from movement.

image.alt: FBC agent Zoe De Vera speaking with Dylan Faden
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot of Zoe De Vera, Dylan's FBC handler.

sections.title: The combat resource loop
paragraphs: The Aberrant handles close-range pressure, while Combat Abilities provide paranatural control. Landing melee attacks restores the resource used by Combat Abilities. Those abilities can inflict Falter, opening an enemy to an execution, and executions temporarily strengthen melee attacks.

That creates a deliberate loop: engage with a Weapon Form, spend restored power on an ability, exploit Falter with an execution, then use the melee boost to stay aggressive. The exact route changes with the chosen Forms, abilities, and Talents.
bullets: Melee hits replenish Combat Ability power.
Combat Abilities can control space, inflict status effects, or build Falter.
Faltered enemies can be executed.
Executions grant a temporary melee damage boost.
Mold Turrets and summoned Seekers can act independently while Dylan fights.

image.alt: Dylan using a paranatural power during a Manhattan combat encounter
image.caption: Official screenshot. Combat Abilities complement the Aberrant rather than replacing melee combat.

rows: The Aberrant's moveset, range, and combo role
Active paranatural powers earned from Resonants
Dodge Attack node shown by Remedy
table.caption: Four connected build systems

image.alt: CONTROL Resonant loadout screen showing the Seekers summon ability and detailed statistics
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog image. Remedy exposes detailed values for loadout comparison.

sections.title: What is The Gap?
paragraphs: The Gap is a dreamlike space connected to Dylan. It functions as the visual home for buildcrafting: players access it with the directional pad to review and change parts of the loadout.

Untapped Artifacts can also be shaped into usable Artifacts in The Gap. Remedy has not described The Gap as a normal Manhattan district, so it is best understood as a progression and loadout space with narrative meaning.

image.alt: Dylan standing in the blue dreamlike space known as The Gap
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot of The Gap, the game's buildcrafting space.

sections.title: Bosses change the build
paragraphs: Resonants are major paranatural entities and central boss encounters. Defeating one unlocks a unique Combat Ability, with branching choices that can produce different rewards from the same boss across playthroughs.
New Game Plus expands this idea with new Talent nodes and alternative ability choices. That makes bosses part of progression rather than isolated set pieces.

image.alt: A multi-armed Resonant entity in CONTROL Resonant
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog screenshot of a Resonant encounter. Remedy has not published a canonical boss name for this entity.

title: Is CONTROL Resonant Single-Player or Multiplayer?
excerpt: The official answer on single-player, co-op, offline play, and why FBC: Firebreak is a different CONTROL universe game.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant is sometimes confused with Remedy's cooperative FBC: Firebreak. Remedy's developer FAQ gives an unambiguous answer about Resonant's player count and internet requirement.
quickAnswer: CONTROL Resonant is a single-player game. It has no announced cooperative or competitive multiplayer mode, and Remedy says the game can be played offline without an internet connection.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden standing alone beneath a towering structure in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: Official multiplayer answer
paragraphs: The PlayStation Store also lists the game as one-player, matching Remedy's developer-pinned Steam FAQ.

sections.title: What the single-player campaign contains
paragraphs: The campaign follows Dylan Faden as he searches for his missing sister Jesse during a paranatural crisis in Manhattan. Its structure combines the main storyline, called Dylan's Journey, with optional World Quests, bounties, collectibles, bosses, puzzles, and hidden encounters.
Zoe De Vera acts as Dylan's FBC handler, but she is a story character rather than a second player character. Nothing in Remedy's official material describes drop-in co-op, PvP, or shared-world play.

sections.title: Can you play offline?
paragraphs: Yes. Remedy's FAQ says CONTROL Resonant does not require an internet connection to play. A platform can still require an initial download, installation, account verification, or updates depending on the format and storefront, but the game itself is described as offline-capable.

sections.title: How this differs from FBC: Firebreak
paragraphs: FBC: Firebreak is Remedy's three-player cooperative first-person game set in the CONTROL universe. CONTROL Resonant is the direct single-player sequel to CONTROL and uses a third-person action-RPG format.
The shared universe and FBC setting do not make the two games the same type of experience. Buying or playing Resonant does not provide a cooperative campaign.

sections.title: Could multiplayer be added later?
paragraphs: Remedy says the game is designed as a complete experience at launch and that future plans will be shared later. No multiplayer expansion has been announced. Until Remedy says otherwise, listings that promise future co-op should be treated as speculation.

title: CONTROL Resonant Steam Deck Support Explained
excerpt: What Remedy has confirmed for Steam Deck, what Valve verification means, and the PC requirements that still matter.
introduction: Remedy has answered the Steam Deck question directly, but 'supported' and Valve's store badge are not identical claims. Here is the confirmed status without predicting performance.
quickAnswer: Remedy says CONTROL Resonant supports Steam Deck at launch. A final Valve Verified or Playable badge, frame-rate target, graphics preset, and battery-life estimate were not specified in the official FAQ checked for this guide.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden fighting with a scythe-like Aberrant form in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: Steam Deck status
paragraphs: The confirmation appears in a developer-pinned FAQ on Steam. It is stronger evidence than an unsupported compatibility estimate, but it does not publish a performance benchmark.

sections.title: Support is not the same as Valve verification
paragraphs: Remedy controls the game's support statement. Valve assigns the separate Verified, Playable, Unsupported, or Unknown compatibility label shown by Steam after testing.
A game can be supported by its developer before Valve displays a final badge. For the current badge, always check the Steam store or the compatibility detail screen on the Deck.

sections.title: What has not been promised
bullets: No official Steam Deck frame-rate target was included in the FAQ.
No native resolution or upscaling mode was specified for the handheld.
No battery-life estimate has been published.
No statement promises path tracing or the highest PC settings on Steam Deck hardware.

sections.title: Storage, controls, and saves
paragraphs: The final PC requirements list 120 GB of SSD storage, so available space is the first practical Deck check. Steam lists full controller support and Steam Cloud. Remedy separately confirms Xbox controllers and the PlayStation 5 DualSense controller on PC.
The Steam page lists Family Sharing and HDR support as PC features. Their availability does not guarantee that every feature behaves identically on SteamOS.

sections.title: A reliable launch-day checklist
bullets: Install current SteamOS and game updates.
Read Valve's compatibility notes, not only the badge color.
Keep more than 120 GB free for installation overhead and updates.
Start with conservative graphics settings until measured Deck benchmarks are available.
Use cloud saves only after confirming a completed sync before switching PCs.

title: CONTROL Resonant Assist Mode and Accessibility Settings
excerpt: Every officially revealed Assist Mode control, PlayStation accessibility tag, and trophy rule in one verified guide.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant expands the original game's Assist Mode with granular sliders and toggles that can make combat easier or harder. Remedy says these settings can be changed at any time and do not disable trophies or achievements.
quickAnswer: Assist Mode includes controls for enemy aggression, dodge timing, projectile speed, incoming and outgoing damage, Falter, power recovery, melee magnetizing, immortality, one-hit kills, and one-hit Falters. No trophy or achievement is locked behind a difficulty setting.
imageAlt: CONTROL Resonant Assist Mode settings screen

sections.title: How Assist Mode works
paragraphs: Players can choose a preset and then fine-tune individual options. The controls are bidirectional where relevant, so they can reduce pressure or deliberately create a harder custom setup.

rows: Timing leniency for a perfect dodge
How quickly Dylan builds enemy Falter
How quickly Combat Ability power returns
Defeats applicable enemies in one hit
Immediately opens applicable enemies to Falter
table.caption: All confirmed Assist Mode settings

image.alt: Assist Mode menu with adjustable combat settings in CONTROL Resonant
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog screenshot. Settings shown before release may receive wording or value changes through updates.

sections.title: Assist Mode does not block trophies
paragraphs: Remedy states that no trophy or achievement is gated by difficulty or Assist Mode. Players can adjust settings during a playthrough without sacrificing platform completion rewards.
That policy makes options such as Immortality and One-Hit Kills usable for access needs, time constraints, or replay convenience rather than treating them as a separate non-progression mode.

sections.title: Accessibility features listed on PlayStation Store
paragraphs: The PlayStation Store currently displays nine accessibility feature tags. Store tags are broad categories, so the exact in-game implementation should be checked in the settings menu at launch.
bullets: Separate volume controls and mono audio
Subtitles and large-subtitle options
Advanced controller remapping
Stick sensitivity and inversion controls
Advanced adjustable difficulty
The ability to pause the game

sections.title: Useful ways to tune the game
paragraphs: These are practical starting points inferred from the function of the official settings, not Remedy-authored presets.
bullets: For reaction-time support: slow projectiles and widen the Perfect Dodge Window.
For lower motor demand: enable Enhanced Melee Magnetizing and increase outgoing Falter.
For reduced punishment: lower incoming damage or enable Immortality while leaving enemy behavior intact.
For a harder replay: increase enemy aggression and incoming damage while narrowing dodge timing.

sections.title: Accessibility details still to verify
paragraphs: The official material checked here does not provide a full launch menu for color-vision filters, screen-reader coverage, hold-versus-toggle options, camera shake, motion blur, or puzzle assistance. Those details should not be assumed from Assist Mode alone.

title: CONTROL Resonant New Game Plus: What Carries Over
excerpt: Confirmed NG+ carryover, traversal reset, fourth Artifact slot, new Talents, harder enemies, and replayable choices.
introduction: New Game Plus is more than a stat carryover mode in CONTROL Resonant. Remedy says it adds progression options, changes encounters, and lets players pursue alternative ability and story outcomes.
quickAnswer: NG+ carries over Aberrant upgrades, health and Combat Ability resource improvements, unlocked abilities, Talents, and Artifacts. Story-gated traversal abilities reset. NG+ adds new Talent nodes, a fourth Artifact slot, tougher evolving enemies, and opportunities to make different quest and boss-reward choices.
imageAlt: Dylan facing a fiery Resonant entity in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: What changes in CONTROL Resonant New Game Plus?
paragraphs: Remedy revealed NG+ before launch but did not attach a separate release date to the mode in the article. The official explanation presents it as a designed replay path rather than a simple restart with higher numbers.

sections.title: What carries over
bullets: Aberrant upgrades and unlocked Weapon Form progression
Health improvements
Combat Ability resource improvements
Combat Abilities already earned
Unlocked Talents
Collected and crafted Artifacts

sections.title: What does not carry over
paragraphs: Traversal abilities tied to story progression do not carry into NG+. Remedy says this preserves the intended sequence of exploration and prevents late-game movement tools from breaking early progression.
That means a fully upgraded combat build can return, while access to certain locations still follows the campaign's traversal unlocks.

sections.title: New Talents and a fourth Artifact slot
paragraphs: NG+ introduces Talent nodes unavailable in the first run. It also unlocks a fourth Artifact slot; the first playthrough provides three.

Artifacts can affect survivability, combat, exploration, or resource economy. Some include activation conditions or tradeoffs, so the extra slot can change build behavior rather than adding only a flat bonus.

image.alt: CONTROL Resonant Talent screen with Primary, Secondary, and Combo Ender branches
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog image of the Talent interface. NG+ adds further Talent nodes.

sections.title: Different rewards from the same Resonant
paragraphs: Major Resonants can offer branching Combat Ability rewards. NG+ lets players return with one ability from a boss and pursue another choice, expanding the available loadout without discarding the first run's reward.
Remedy has not published a complete boss-to-ability table, so individual reward names should be treated as unknown unless shown in official footage or the released game.

image.alt: A major multi-armed Resonant boss in CONTROL Resonant
image.caption: Resonants are major bosses that grant branching Combat Ability choices.

sections.title: How the world changes in NG+
paragraphs: Enemies become harder and can evolve. Remedy says some bosses gain new behaviors, creating encounters that are not identical to the first run.
World Quests, bounties, and collectibles can be revisited. Different choices may lead to changed outcomes or conversations, though Remedy has not promised that every quest branches.

sections.title: First-run preparation
bullets: Finish optional World Quests if you want more first-run context before changing choices.
Collect Untapped Artifacts and shape them in The Gap to widen the NG+ build pool.
Record which Combat Ability branch you select after a Resonant fight.
Do not plan an NG+ route around keeping every traversal power from the finale.

title: CONTROL Resonant Combat Abilities and Aberrant Forms
excerpt: Six named preview Weapon Forms, Barrage, Seekers, Shield, status effects, Talents and the combat loop.
introduction: Dylan does not use Jesse's transforming Service Weapon. His central tool is the Aberrant, a shape-changing paranatural melee weapon supported by Combat Abilities earned from Resonants.
quickAnswer: Xbox Wire's first-party hands-on names Flurry, Slash and Slice as opening Primary Forms, then Crush, Drill and Extend as Secondary choices. It also describes Barrage, Seekers and Shield as three early Resonant reward options. These are preview-build options, not a complete retail Form or ability list.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden wielding the massive hammer form of the Aberrant

facts.label: Named preview Forms
facts.value: Flurry / Slash / Slice; Crush / Drill / Extend

sections.title: Confirmed combat toolkit
paragraphs: The combat system comes from Remedy's published explanation. Xbox Wire's hands-on identifies six Form names and three ability choices in an opening-hour preview; their labels are useful, but their preview values are not final balance data.

sections.title: The Aberrant and Weapon Forms
paragraphs: The Aberrant is Dylan's transforming melee weapon. Remedy officially shows a crushing hammer and fast dual-blade configuration and says additional forms support different playstyles.

Weapon Forms feed three Talent areas shown in the official interface: Primary, Secondary, and Combo Enders. Players combine their choices rather than committing to one fixed weapon for the entire game.

image.alt: Dylan using a long scythe-like Aberrant configuration
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot. The image shows a long-bladed form; the storefront does not publish its canonical name.

sections.title: Six named Forms in the opening preview
paragraphs: Xbox Wire's first-party hands-on reports a starting choice between Flurry, Slash and Slice. Later the demo offers Crush, Drill and Extend as Secondary choices. The writer describes their roles—quick daggers, group-covering scythe, positional axe, heavy mallet, sustained Drill and longer-reaching chain staff.

Game Informer also described Combo Ender attacks, but neither preview establishes a complete retail menu or final upgrade values. Choose by the encounter problem you want a Form to solve, not by an untested damage ranking.

rows: Fast close-range / crowd-wide / single-target with rear bonus
Heavy mallet / sustained damage / extra reach
Finishing attacks chosen separately from Primary and Secondary
table.caption: Weapon Forms named in the June 11 first-party hands-on

sections.title: Seekers summon
paragraphs: An official loadout screenshot names Seekers as a summon Combat Ability. The displayed description calls it a telekinetic entity, and the interface shows that Seekers can be thrown or detonated.

The same screen exposes duration, damage, health, damage resistance, power cost, recovery, detonation damage, and upgrade values. Those visible statistics support detailed build comparison without relying on vague rarity labels.

image.alt: Seekers summon statistics in the CONTROL Resonant loadout menu
image.caption: Official pre-release loadout screenshot. Exact numeric values may be balanced by launch updates.

sections.title: Mold Turrets and status effects
paragraphs: Remedy uses Mold Turrets as an example of a Combat Ability that keeps acting after it is placed. The turrets independently attack enemies and apply status effects, allowing Dylan to continue a melee sequence elsewhere.
The official deep dive frames abilities as tools for crowd control, Falter buildup, and build synergy, not only as direct-damage cooldowns.

image.alt: Dylan using a Combat Ability that creates a bright status effect
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog combat screenshot. The exact ability name in this frame was not provided.

sections.title: Talents modify the moveset
paragraphs: Talents sit alongside Forms rather than replacing them. An official interface screenshot shows a Dodge Attack node requiring Aberrant Strength and a branching network across Primary, Secondary, and Combo Ender tabs.
New Game Plus adds further Talent nodes. Remedy has not released a complete launch tree, so a full build calculator would be premature.

image.alt: CONTROL Resonant Talent tree showing a Dodge Attack upgrade
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog Talent screen with pre-release UI and values.

sections.title: How to think about a loadout
paragraphs: A strong loadout needs a way to enter melee range, restore ability power, apply Falter or another status, execute vulnerable targets, and use the resulting melee boost. Summons or deployables can cover space while a different Aberrant form handles the active target.
This is a system-level recommendation based on Remedy's published combat loop. Exact best-in-slot combinations should wait for final damage values and enemy behavior.

title: How Long Is CONTROL Resonant?
excerpt: Remedy estimates 25–35 hours for the main story; an earlier developer interview estimated roughly 30 hours for the core experience and 50 for completionists.
introduction: Two pre-release Remedy statements use different playtime labels. This page keeps the main-story range separate from the broader core and completion estimates instead of treating them as stopwatch results.
quickAnswer: Remedy's September 15 PS5 briefing estimates 25–35 hours for the main story, with more time for completionists. An earlier lead-designer interview put the core experience around 30 hours and completionist play around 50. These are planning estimates, not measured retail averages.
imageAlt: Dylan traversing a towering environment reshaped by a Gravity Anomaly

sections.title: How long is the main story?
paragraphs: Remedy's September 15 PS5 briefing estimates 25 to 35 hours for the main story, with additional time for completionists. A separate interview with lead gameplay designer Sergey Mohov describes roughly 30 hours for the core experience and around 50 hours for completionist play. These are different scopes, not a promise of one exact completion time.

sections.title: What does the 30-hour core estimate include?
paragraphs: Mohov called 30 hours the core experience rather than publishing a main-story speedrun time. Remedy separately describes the game as its largest production and says Manhattan contains branching missions, encounters, events, secrets, and World Quests.
Because the two sources use different terms, this site does not translate 'core experience' into an exact main-story-only number.

sections.title: What can push the game toward 50 hours
bullets: Narrative World Quests away from Dylan's Journey
Hidden encounters and optional discoveries in each zone
Environmental puzzles and Gravity Anomalies
Bounties and collectibles
Artifact hunting and loadout experimentation
Exploration after new traversal abilities unlock routes

sections.title: New Game Plus is additional time
paragraphs: The 50-hour completion estimate should not automatically be read as a full NG+ completion. NG+ carries combat progression forward, adds Talent nodes and a fourth Artifact slot, changes some enemy and boss behavior, and allows different quest or ability choices.
A second comprehensive run can therefore extend well beyond the first-playthrough estimate. Remedy has not given a separate average for NG+.

sections.title: Why your time may differ
paragraphs: Assist Mode can alter enemy aggression, damage, Falter, power recovery, dodge timing, and other combat variables. Difficulty tuning, reading lore, repeated build changes, and exploration habits all affect playtime.
The safest expectation is a substantial single-player RPG campaign, not an exact timer.

sections.title: Time needed to catch up on CONTROL
paragraphs: The same interview says CONTROL Resonant includes a CONTROL recap accessible from the top of the main menu. New players can use it instead of completing the entire original game first, although playing CONTROL provides more context for Dylan, Jesse, the Hiss, and the Oldest House.

title: CONTROL Resonant Characters, Cast & Story Setup
excerpt: Meet Dylan, Jesse and Zoe, plus the actors and returning FBC characters revealed in Remedy's September cast diary. Casting spoilers are labeled.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant shifts the playable role from Jesse to Dylan Faden and moves the crisis into Manhattan. This guide explains only the officially published setup and avoids presenting trailer imagery as a solved plot.
quickAnswer: Dylan Faden is the protagonist. He enters a warped Manhattan after receiving a message from Jesse, who is missing. FBC agent Zoe De Vera acts as his handler. A new resonance has altered reality while the Hiss and Mold are also present.
imageAlt: Zoe De Vera speaking to Dylan Faden in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: Spoiler-light story premise
paragraphs: CONTROL Resonant takes place after CONTROL and is a direct sequel. Remedy also designed it as an entry point, and a developer interview confirms that the main menu includes a recap of the first game.

sections.title: Dylan Faden
paragraphs: Dylan was central to CONTROL's story but was not its playable hero. In Resonant, he leaves years of Bureau confinement behind and takes the lead during a crisis that may also be his path toward redemption.
His connection to paranatural forces is expressed through the Aberrant and Combat Abilities. Remedy's public setup does not reveal his final motives or the full circumstances of his release.

image.alt: Dylan Faden carrying the Aberrant over a transformed Manhattan
image.caption: Official CONTROL Resonant key art featuring protagonist Dylan Faden.

sections.title: Jesse Faden
paragraphs: Jesse was the protagonist of CONTROL and became Director of the Federal Bureau of Control. Resonant begins with Jesse missing and Dylan responding to a message from her.
Remedy has not explained where Jesse is, whether the message is reliable, or how large her on-screen role will be. Those questions are part of the sequel's mystery, not confirmed answers.

sections.title: Zoe De Vera
paragraphs: Zoe De Vera is an FBC field agent and Dylan's handler. Official gameplay material shows her communicating with Dylan while he explores, with conversations designed to flow without repeatedly stopping the player.
Her presence connects field operations in Manhattan to the Bureau without making her a cooperative player character.

image.alt: Zoe De Vera and Dylan Faden in an official CONTROL Resonant scene
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot of Zoe De Vera with Dylan.

sections.title: Official cast reveals — returning-character spoilers
paragraphs: The September 10 Meet the Cast diary confirms additional returning characters. This table reveals casting, not where or how each person appears in the campaign.

table.caption: Actors and characters in the development diary

sections.title: The new resonance, Hiss, and Mold
paragraphs: Remedy describes an unprecedented paranatural crisis driven by a mysterious new resonance. The returning Hiss and Mold are also present, but official launch copy treats them as part of a changed threat landscape rather than proof that CONTROL's original conflict simply repeats.
Resonants are major entities Dylan hunts and defeats. They grant Combat Ability choices, connecting the narrative threat directly to progression.

image.alt: Two different paranatural hostile entities in CONTROL Resonant
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog screenshot. Enemy taxonomy should remain provisional until names appear in the released database.

sections.title: What newcomers need to know
paragraphs: The FBC investigates and contains paranatural events and objects. The Oldest House is its shifting headquarters. Jesse and Dylan are siblings whose childhood encounter with a paranatural event shaped their lives and the first game's conflict.
That foundation is enough to understand the public setup. The built-in recap can fill in essential history, while the original game remains the richer route for character context.

title: CONTROL Resonant PC Features, Languages, and Controls
excerpt: Steam features, controller support, localized audio and subtitles, GeForce technology, offline play, and platform differences.
introduction: The PC version spans multiple storefronts and a wide range of hardware. This reference collects confirmed user-facing features without treating optional RTX technology as a universal requirement.
quickAnswer: On Steam, CONTROL Resonant lists achievements, trading cards, cloud saves, HDR, Family Sharing, full controller support, 15 interface and subtitle languages, and eight full-audio languages. Remedy confirms offline play, Xbox and PS5 DualSense controllers, and Steam Deck support at launch.
imageAlt: Official CONTROL Resonant PC performance requirements chart

sections.title: What PC graphics and control features are confirmed?
paragraphs: Feature labels can differ between Steam, Epic, Xbox on PC, and the future Mac release. The detailed list on this page refers to Steam unless a section names another source.

sections.title: Steam features
bullets: Single-player campaign
Steam Achievements and Steam Trading Cards
Steam Cloud
HDR support
Family Sharing
Full controller support
Steam Deck support confirmed separately by Remedy

sections.title: Controller support on PC
paragraphs: Remedy's FAQ names Xbox controllers and the PlayStation 5 DualSense controller as supported on PC. PlayStation's console listing separately advertises DualSense vibration and trigger effects on PS5.
The official material checked here does not promise that every PS5-specific haptic effect is reproduced identically over every PC connection method.

sections.title: Steam language support

rows: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish (Spain), Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil), Simplified Chinese
Korean, Polish, Russian, Spanish (Latin America), Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian
table.caption: Steam language support

paragraphs: Store language tables can change through release and patches. Check the storefront immediately before purchasing if a particular dub or text localization is essential.

sections.title: NVIDIA graphics features
paragraphs: NVIDIA says the PC version supports DLSS 4.5 Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, path tracing, and RTX Mega Geometry on compatible GeForce RTX hardware.

These are scalable features, not the baseline PC requirement. The official minimum tier starts with a GTX 1070, RX 5600 XT, or Arc A580 for 1080p at 30 FPS using the Low preset with Quality upscaling.

sections.title: Offline play and accounts
paragraphs: Remedy says an internet connection is not required to play. A storefront account and internet access can still be necessary to purchase, download, update, synchronize cloud saves, or verify ownership during installation.
Steam Cloud and GeForce NOW are online conveniences, not evidence that the campaign is online-only.

sections.title: Mac timing
paragraphs: The Mac version is planned for later in 2026 through Steam and the Mac App Store. Remedy has not announced a precise Mac date in the launch article. Windows specifications should not be reused as unverified Mac requirements.
